title: Login with email and password
text: Open the Login screen and enter your email and password. Tap Login to continue. If login is successful, the app opens your main home flow. If the credentials are wrong, you will stay on the login flow and see an error from the auth process.

title: Login with Google or Apple
text: You can use social sign-in from the authentication flow. The app supports Google and Apple sign-in and then continues with the same user session logic as email login. If social authentication fails, retry from the same login screen.

title: Registration required fields
text: Registration validates email format and password rules before sending data. Password must be at least 6 characters and confirmation must match. You also need to accept Terms of Use to create an account.

title: Terms acceptance during registration
text: If Terms of Use are not accepted, registration cannot continue. Enable the terms checkbox and submit again. This is a required step in the registration flow.

title: Email verification code flow
text: After registration, email verification is handled by a code confirmation screen. Enter the verification code to confirm your email. If the code was not received or expired, use the resend code action and try again.

title: Email is required error
text: If email is empty, the app shows a required-email validation message. Enter a valid email address and submit again. The same validation is used in login and registration flows.

title: Invalid email format error
text: If the email format is incorrect, the app blocks submit and asks for a valid email. Update the email field to a standard address format. Then retry login or registration.

title: Password minimum length
text: Password must contain at least 6 characters. If the password is shorter, registration cannot continue. Update the password and submit again.

title: Password confirmation mismatch
text: If password and confirmation do not match, the app shows a mismatch message and blocks registration. Re-enter both fields with the same value. Then submit again.

title: How logout works
text: Logout is available from the Profile flow. When you sign out, the app clears session data and returns to the start/login path. After logout, protected user actions require sign-in again.

title: Location disclosure before permission
text: Before runtime location permission, the app shows a location disclosure dialog. If user selects Not now, permission request is not sent in that step. User can continue app flow with limited location-dependent actions.

title: Location permission during startup
text: During startup, the app requests location permission after disclosure. If permission is granted, location service initialization continues. If permission is denied, location-dependent features stay limited until permission is granted later.

title: Location service is disabled
text: If device location service is off, the app shows a warning that executor actions are limited. The warning includes an action to open device location settings. Enable location service in system settings and return to the app.

title: Open location settings action
text: In the location-off warning, tap the button to open device location settings directly. Turn location services on, then return to the app. The app re-checks location state when resumed.

title: Startup behavior when location service is off
text: If permission exists but system location service is turned off, startup does not keep waiting for real coordinates. This avoids long waiting after splash. User can still continue and enable location later from warning/settings.

title: Why executor actions are blocked without location
text: Without location permission or enabled location service, users can still donate and create requests, but executor actions are restricted. Joining and performing tasks requires location checks. Enable permission and device location service to unlock executor actions.

title: How to create a waste cleanup request
text: From the main screen, tap the "+" button and select request type "Waste Cleanup" (Waste Location). Fill required fields: location, title, and description, then add required photos and waste details (size/type/access). Submit the request and wait for success confirmation.

title: Waste cleanup requires selected location
text: If location is not selected, creation shows a location-required error and does not submit. Pick a map location first, then submit again. This is a hard validation step.

title: How to create a speed cleanup
text: Open Speed Cleanup creation and fill required fields, including location and cleanup details. Add required cleanup photos in the flow. Submit and wait for creation success message.

title: Speed cleanup photo requirements
text: Speed cleanup flow uses before/after photo logic in creation and completion-related UI. If required photos are missing, the app asks to add them before submission. Add photos and retry submit.

title: How to create an event request
text: Open Event creation and fill required fields like location, title, description, and event date/time. Add event photos as needed by the form. Submit creation and confirm success message.

title: Event creation date and time requirement
text: Event creation requires selecting date and time as part of the form flow. If this is missing, creation cannot finish correctly. Set event schedule fields and submit again.

title: Please fill all required fields error
text: When required request fields are missing, the app shows a fill-required message. Review all required inputs on the current creation screen. Complete missing fields and submit again.

title: Request creation failed
text: If request creation fails, the app shows an error and keeps you in the creation flow. Check required fields, internet connection, and try submit again. Retry from the same screen is supported.

title: How to join a request
text: Open request details and use the Join action if available. On success, the app shows a join-success message and updates participation state. If join fails, retry and verify location-related requirements.

title: How to cancel participation (unjoin)
text: From request details, use the Unjoin action to cancel your participation. On success, app shows unjoin confirmation and updates state. If unjoin fails, retry from the same request details screen.

title: How to join an event
text: Open event details and tap Join when event participation is open. Success is confirmed by event-join success feedback. If joining is canceled later, app shows event-canceled participation feedback.

title: Event has not started yet
text: If you try to perform event actions too early, the app can show that event has not started yet. Wait until the event start time, then retry perform/completion actions. This is an expected time-based restriction.

title: Event distance restriction for task actions
text: Event perform flow checks distance to event location. If you are outside the allowed radius, app shows a distance restriction message and blocks the action. Move closer to the event location and retry.

title: Out of cleanup radius message
text: During cleanup-related actions, app can show that you are out of allowed cleanup radius. Return to the task location and try again. This check protects location-based task completion flow.

title: How participant completion submission works
text: Participant completion flow requires submitting cleanup result data, including after-photo evidence in relevant screens. After submit, request moves to review-dependent state. If submission fails, app shows retry-oriented error feedback.

title: Cannot complete without after photo
text: If after photo is required and missing, completion flow asks to add it first. Upload the after photo and submit completion again. This is a common reason for completion submit failure.

title: Request ID is missing in completion flow
text: If completion screen cannot resolve request ID, submission is blocked and app shows a missing request ID error. Reopen completion from the request details flow instead of stale navigation entry. Then retry submission.

title: Completion submit failed
text: When work completion submit fails, app shows an error and advises retry. Check network stability and try again from the same completion screen. If issue repeats, reopen request details and retry flow.

title: What pending review status means
text: Pending status means request or completion is waiting for moderation/review stage. It is not final approved/rejected result yet. Wait for status update or creator/admin decision depending on flow.

title: What in progress status means
text: In Progress means active execution is ongoing and not finished. Continue work from request details if continue action is available. Submit completion when task result is ready.

title: What approved status means
text: Approved status indicates review accepted the result for that flow. Approved is a positive final or near-final moderation outcome. Related actions may become limited after approval depending on screen logic.

title: What rejected status means
text: Rejected status means review declined submitted result. In participant moderation flows, rejection can include a rejection reason. Check details and follow available next actions in the request screen.

title: What completed status means
text: Completed status means the task/request reached its completion state in the app flow. Completed requests usually have no active executor actions left. Open details to review final data and outcome.

title: Why request may not be visible (archived)
text: Archived requests are filtered from standard active request views in app repositories. If a request is archived, it may not appear in normal browsing lists. Open direct details link or related history/admin views if available to inspect it.

title: How to send a donation to an existing request
text: To send money to support someone else's cleanup, you do not need to create your own request first. Pick any existing request on the map or list, open its details screen, and tap Donate. That starts the in-app Stripe payment flow and shows success feedback when it completes. Receiving donated funds on your balance as a performer is a different flow: complete the work, pass verification/moderation as the app shows, and connect Stripe in your profile to withdraw.

title: Minimum donation amount
text: Minimum donation amount is $1.00 in the app. If amount is below minimum, donation flow will not continue. Increase amount to at least $1.00 and retry.

title: Donation payment failed
text: If donation payment creation fails, app shows payment failed feedback and keeps you in current flow. Retry donation from request details. If cancellation happened manually, app shows payment canceled state.

title: Stripe setup requirement for receiving donation money
text: App warns that without fully configured Stripe account and linked debit card, donation money payouts are not available as expected. Complete Stripe setup from profile-related payment section. Then retry payout-related actions.

title: Payout screen tabs
text: Payouts page has two tabs: Available and History. Available shows current amounts and payout action, while History lists past payout records. Use these tabs to understand current and past payout states.

title: Instant payout minimum amount
text: Instant payout is available only from $1.00 and above. For lower amounts, app indicates scheduled transfer behavior. If instant payout button does not complete, check your amount and payout method availability.

title: No funds available for payout
text: If balance is not available, app shows no-funds message in payout flow. In this state, payout action cannot proceed. Wait for eligible balance updates and retry later.

title: No payout methods available
text: If no payout method is linked, app shows no payout methods message in instant payout flow. Add/enable payout method in Stripe setup path first. Then return to payouts and retry.

title: How to open chat and send a message
text: Open chat from chat list or supported route, then enter text and tap Send. Empty messages are ignored by input validation. Sent messages appear in the conversation with sender-side bubble styling.

title: Why empty message is not sent
text: The chat input trims text and blocks empty messages. If message is only spaces or blank, send action does nothing. Enter text content and send again.

title: Typing indicator behavior in chat
text: Chat screen can show a typing indicator when typing events are present from participants. Indicator appears as someone typing text in chat UI. It is transient and depends on live chat state updates.

title: How chat read state updates on open
text: When you open a chat, the app marks the chat as read and resets unread count for that chat. This uses chat read endpoints in the backend integration. If unread badge stays stale, reopen the same chat and return to chat list.

title: Read receipt icon on your messages
text: For your own messages, chat bubble shows check icons based on read-by data. Single check and double-check visuals are used in UI for delivery/read style feedback. Exact recipient read timing depends on server updates.

title: Unread badge in chat list
text: Chat list shows unread counters per chat and updates counts from chat state. Opening a chat usually clears that chat unread count. Very large counters are compacted in badge display logic.

title: Invalid chat route behavior
text: If chat route is opened without a valid chat ID, chat page cannot initialize proper conversation context. Use valid chat link/route with chatId parameter. Reopen from in-app chat list when possible.

title: Private chat not found
text: If app cannot resolve private chat for the current context, it can show private chat not found message. Reopen the related request/details flow and try chat action again. If still missing, the chat relation may not exist yet.

title: How to open and review notifications
text: Notifications page shows your notification list with pagination and refresh options. Tap any notification card to open details in a bottom sheet. Opening a card also marks that notification as read.

title: Mark all notifications as read
text: If there are unread notifications, use the done-all action in notifications app bar. App calls mark-all-read and updates local notification list state. A success snackbar confirms all marked as read.

title: Refresh notifications and retry load
text: Notifications page supports pull-to-refresh and refresh icon in app bar. If loading fails, error state includes retry action. Use refresh/retry to fetch latest notifications again.

title: No notifications yet
text: If there are no notifications, app shows an empty notifications state. This is expected when your account has no recent notification records. You can return later and refresh.

title: Push notification permission basics
text: Push service initialization requests system notification permission and configures foreground/local handling. If permission is denied, push delivery visibility is limited by OS settings. Enable notifications in device settings and relaunch app.

title: Push on devices without Google Play Services
text: FCM token retrieval can fail on devices/emulators without Google Play Services support. In such cases, push notifications may not work as expected. Use a device with proper Google services for reliable FCM behavior.

title: How request deep links open in app
text: Request deep links support both web and app-scheme formats, such as /request/{category}/{requestId}. App parses category and request ID, then opens the matching request details screen. If request is not found, error fallback screen is shown.

title: How news deep links open in app
text: News deep links support /news/{newsId} in web and app-scheme formats. App parses newsId and routes to news details screen. If link format is invalid, parsing fails and no news navigation is performed.

title: Deep link behavior on cold start
text: On cold start, app may queue deep link first and apply it after home route is ready. This prevents splash navigation from overriding deep link target. If it looks delayed, wait until home is initialized.

title: Duplicate deep links are ignored briefly
text: If the same deep link arrives multiple times within a short window, app ignores duplicates to prevent repeated navigation. This is expected anti-duplicate behavior. Use one valid link tap and wait for navigation.

title: Invalid deep link format behavior
text: If deep link format does not match supported request/news patterns, app does not navigate to target content. Invalid format is logged internally and ignored in UI navigation flow. Use a valid deep link structure and retry.

title: Open chat by route link
text: Chat route supports /chat/{chatId} navigation when a valid chatId is provided. If chatId is missing, route cannot open conversation correctly. Use links that include actual chat ID from app context.

title: How to edit profile data
text: Profile edit flow supports user data updates like first name, last name, country, city, about, and social links. Save changes from edit profile screen to update account data. Updated profile is then used in user-facing views.

title: Profile photo update behavior
text: Profile editing flow includes profile image update in user data update process. If image update fails, app can show photo processing or save-related errors. Retry image selection/upload and save again.

title: Open public user profile
text: App supports user profile route with user ID parameter to open public user profile page. If user ID is missing in route, fallback error UI appears. Open user profile from valid in-app links when possible.

title: Language change in profile flow
text: Language settings are available in profile and app localization supports multiple locales. Changing language updates text resources used across screens. Reopen target screen if you need to refresh visible strings immediately.

title: What to do when action fails temporarily
text: For temporary submit/load failures, first retry in the same screen using built-in retry/refresh actions. Then reopen the flow from source screen (request details, chat list, notifications list). If issue persists, capture exact error text and context for support.

title: Why my request is not visible
text: A request can look missing if it is archived or filtered out of active lists. It may also be in status states not shown by your current filter context. Open direct request details link if available and verify status from there.

title: Why I cannot mark request as completed
text: Completion can fail when required proof fields are missing, request ID context is invalid, or location constraints are not satisfied. Check after-photo requirement and distance/time restrictions for your request type. Then retry completion from request details.

title: Why I do not receive notifications
text: Verify OS notification permission for the app and ensure device supports push stack correctly. In-app notifications page can still show records even when push delivery was missed. Use refresh in notifications page and check whether new items appear there.

title: How to open app from deep link
text: Use a valid Joy Pick request or news deep link format. On some cold starts, app may first open splash/home and then navigate to deep link target. If nothing opens, verify link structure and category/request ID values.

title: How chat read status works
text: Opening a chat marks it as read and clears unread count for that chat in list state. For your sent messages, UI check icons are based on read-by metadata from backend responses. Read timing can vary with real-time sync and connection state.

title: You need to sign in before protected actions
text: Some actions require an authenticated session. If auth token is missing or session ended, app asks you to sign in first. Log in again and retry the action.

title: Email not found during login
text: If login email is not recognized, app can show an email-not-found error. Check the entered address and try again. If this is a new account, use registration flow first.

title: Forgot password entry point
text: Password reset flow is available from authentication routing. If user cannot log in with current password, open reset password screen from auth flow and complete reset steps there. After reset, sign in with the new password.

title: Recover after location permission denied
text: If location permission was denied, location-dependent actions stay restricted. Re-trigger permission from relevant flow or use app/device settings to grant location access. Then reopen the action that previously failed.

title: Why map may show cached or default location
text: Location service can use cached coordinates and has fallback behavior when real location is not yet available. In fallback cases, location may not match current position immediately. Enable location service and wait for a fresh update.

title: Join request failed troubleshooting
text: If join action fails, first retry from the same request details page. Then confirm location permission and location service are enabled, because executor actions depend on location checks. If issue persists, reopen request details and retry join.

title: Unjoin request failed troubleshooting
text: If unjoin action fails, keep the current request open and retry once. If it still fails, reopen request details from list/map and try again. This helps resync current participation state before action call.

title: What Continue Work means
text: Continue Work appears when your task already started and remains active. It returns you to active execution flow instead of starting from zero. Use it to resume unfinished work.

title: What Cancel Work does
text: Cancel Work stops your active work state for that task flow. App asks for confirmation because progress can be lost. Use this only if you want to stop current execution.

title: Group chat not found from request
text: If app cannot resolve request group chat, it can show group-chat-not-found message. Reopen request details and retry chat action. If still unavailable, group chat may not be created for that context.

title: Rejection reason is required in participant review
text: In participant moderation reject flow, rejection reason is required. If reason is empty, reject action should not proceed correctly. Enter reason text and submit rejection again.

title: Work completed and sent for moderation
text: After successful completion submit in relevant flows, app can show that work is sent for moderation. This means result is submitted and now waiting for review. Final status update appears after moderation decision.

title: Work completed and waiting for creator approval
text: Some completion flows show waiting for creator approval instead of immediate finalization. In this state, participant should wait for creator decision. Check request status later for approved or rejected outcome.

title: Extend request for one day
text: Request details include an extend action for one day where supported. If extension succeeds, app shows confirmation feedback. Use it when additional execution time is needed.

title: Close request and submit for review
text: Creator-side close action can move request into review submission stage. App confirms this with a submitted-for-review style message. After that, final review outcome updates status later.

title: User canceled donation payment
text: If payment sheet is closed or canceled by user, app treats donation as canceled and shows canceled feedback. No successful donation result is recorded in that attempt. Start donation again when ready.

title: Confirm payout action
text: Instant payout flow requires confirmation after selecting available payout method and amount context. Tap confirm payout to send payout request. Processing state can appear while backend action is running.

title: No payout history yet
text: If no payout records exist, History tab shows an empty state message. This is expected for accounts without completed payouts. Check again after your first successful payout.

title: No chats yet
text: Chat list can show empty state when user has no active chat threads. Start participation or open supported support/request chat flows to generate chats. Refresh chat list after new activity.

title: Message sending in progress
text: When a message is being sent, chat UI shows sending progress on send control. Wait until sending completes before retrying rapid taps. This helps avoid accidental duplicate sends.

title: Why chat title changes by context
text: Chat header can show request name when chat is linked to a request ID. For support/private/group contexts without request data, title falls back to chat type labels. This is expected header behavior.

title: Notification is marked read on detail open
text: When you open notification details modal, app marks that notification as read automatically. You do not need extra button tap for single-item read in this flow. Return to list to see updated read style.

title: Unread indicator on notification card
text: Unread notifications are styled differently and include a visual unread indicator. After read action, card style returns to normal read appearance. This helps quickly scan unread vs read items.

title: Notification load error with retry button
text: If notifications load fails and list is empty, app shows error state with retry control. Tap retry to request notifications again. Use refresh later if data loads but may be outdated.

title: Supported deep link category paths for requests
text: Request deep links support category paths: waste_location, speed_cleanup, and event. If category path is different, parser rejects the link and navigation will not happen. Use one of supported categories in shared links.

title: Deep link request not found fallback
text: When request ID from deep link cannot be loaded, app shows request-not-found fallback screen. This can happen for invalid, removed, or inaccessible request IDs. Verify link ID and open a current request link.

title: User profile route requires user ID
text: User profile route expects a userId parameter. If userId is missing, app renders fallback error state instead of profile data. Open profile from valid in-app user links.

title: Profile tab refreshes payouts and user data
text: When profile tab is opened from main navigation, app triggers user and payout data refresh in background. This helps keep balance/history sections up to date. If data looks stale, re-open profile tab once.

title: Unread news pulse dot behavior
text: Main navigation shows a pulse dot on News tab when unseen news IDs are detected versus saved seen IDs. Opening News tab marks current news list as seen and removes the dot. This is local unread-news indicator behavior.

title: No news yet state
text: If there are no news items available, News screen shows an empty-state message. This is expected when feed has no entries for current locale/time. Refresh later to check new items.

title: Donation actions from news detail
text: News detail text supports donation-related actions like supporting cleanup or donating to participants/volunteer. These actions route to donation-capable flows linked to request/payment logic. If donation fails, use donation troubleshooting chunks.

title: Map search and filter basics
text: Map/listing supports search by title, city, waste type, or user name (including finding requests from a specific creator). Regional filters include All, America, Europe, and Nearby options. If nothing matches, app shows no-requests hint to adjust query or filters.

title: Map legend: my requests, joins, donations
text: Map/list views include legend groups for My Requests, My Joins, and My Donations. These help users understand ownership/participation context quickly. If expected item is absent, verify current filter scope.

title: Map loading and failed-to-load states
text: Request listing can show loading states while fetching requests/events. If fetch fails, app shows failed-to-load feedback. Retry using refresh actions and check network stability.

title: No user activity map state
text: When user has not created, joined, or donated to any requests, map/listing can show a dedicated no-activity message. This is expected for new or inactive accounts. Create/join/donate to populate personal sections.

title: If user reports app stuck after splash
text: A common case is disabled location service during startup-related checks. Current app behavior avoids long wait for real coordinates when system location is off, then shows location warning with settings action. Ask user to enable location service and reopen target action.

title: Minimum context to collect before escalation
text: For repeat failures, collect: exact screen, exact action tapped, full error text, and whether location/notifications permissions are enabled. Also ask if action was retried after reopening the screen. This context maps directly to existing app-level troubleshooting flows.

title: What request types exist and where to browse them
text: If the user asks what requests exist, what request types there are, or what those pins on the map are—this is about catalog/types, not creating a new request. Answer immediately without the create-flow question "which type do you want to create?": Joy Pick has three request types—(1) Waste Location: mark a polluted spot; (2) Speed Cleanup: your own quick cleanup with before/after photos; (3) Event: a scheduled cleanup or gathering with time and participants. Other people's live requests show on the main map and in lists; users can scroll, search, and filter. Use a type-clarifying question only when the user clearly wants to create a new request and did not name a type.

title: Intent alias: only when user wants to create a new request
text: Use this rule only when the user clearly intends to create a new request (e.g. how do I create a request, I want to add a request) and did not name a type. Then ask which type: waste cleanup, speed cleanup, or event; after they answer, give steps for that type only. Do not use this flow for "what requests exist", "what types are there", or "what is on the map"—for those, list the three types and where to browse (see catalog chunk).

title: Why request is pending intent alias
text: If user asks why request is pending, explain that pending means waiting for review/moderation and not a final result yet. User should wait for status transition to approved or rejected. This is expected moderation stage behavior.

title: How to mark completed intent alias
text: If user asks how to mark as completed, direct them to request completion flow and confirm required proof fields are present. Missing after photo, invalid context, or distance restrictions can block completion. Retry from request details after fixing blockers.

title: Deep link not opening intent alias
text: If user says link does not open, verify link format and required IDs first. App supports request/news patterns and may delay deep link navigation on cold start until home is ready. Invalid format or missing IDs leads to no navigation.

title: Notifications not working intent alias
text: If user reports no notifications, verify device notification permission and push capability first. Then check in-app notifications page with refresh to confirm whether records exist. Missing push can coexist with available in-app notification records.

title: Chat read receipts intent alias
text: If user asks about seen/read in chat, explain that opening chat marks unread as read and check icons for own messages depend on read-by data. Real-time sync can affect exact timing of visual updates. Reopen chat to force state refresh if needed.

title: Cannot join request intent alias
text: If user cannot join, check whether location permission and location service are enabled because executor actions depend on location checks. Retry from request details after enabling required settings. If event is not started yet, joining/performing constraints can also apply.

title: Payment failed intent alias
text: If user reports payment failure, map it to donation/Stripe flow and retry from request details or news donation action. Confirm minimum donation amount and whether payment was canceled manually. Use payout/Stripe setup guidance when issue is account-configuration related.

title: Payout not available intent alias
text: If user asks why payout is unavailable, check available balance, instant payout minimum, and payout method setup. No funds or no payout methods are expected blocking states shown by app. After fixing setup or waiting for balance, retry payout action.

title: Profile update failed intent alias
text: If profile changes are not saved, retry from edit profile screen and verify each edited field and image upload result. Photo processing/save errors can block update completion. Reopen profile and retry save after correcting failed fields.

title: Request not visible short-query alias
text: For short user messages like request missing or not shown, check archived/filter/status causes first. Request may be valid but hidden in active list context. Use direct details path or adjust filter scope.

title: App stuck loading intent alias
text: If user reports long loading around splash/startup, check location service state as first high-probability cause. App now avoids long coordinate wait when location is off, then prompts user with location warning/settings action. Ask user to enable location and retry target flow.

title: Chat not opening intent alias
text: If chat does not open, verify chat route context has a valid chatId and related request chat exists. Missing or invalid chat context leads to fallback errors like chat not found. Reopen from in-app chat list or request details chat action.

title: News unread dot intent alias
text: If user asks about red/pulse dot on news tab, explain it marks unseen news compared to locally saved seen IDs. Opening news tab marks current news list as seen and removes the dot. This is expected local unread-news behavior.

title: Map no results intent alias
text: If user sees no requests on map/list, suggest adjusting search text and filters first. Regional/nearby filter scope can hide otherwise valid items. Loading and failed-to-load states should be handled with refresh and retry.

title: First launch: language, account, map, three eco request types
text: After install, choose language and create an account with email, Google, or Apple. The home screen shows a map with eco-related locations. Tap plus (+) to create an initiative. Three formats exist: Waste Location (mark a polluted area), Speed Cleanup (you mark the place, before/after photos, your cleanup), and Event (planned cleanups, tree planting, etc., with time and participants).

title: Waste Location: polluted spot, donation, optional haul-only
text: Waste Location marks a polluted area. User adds a photo, description, and can attach a donation. Donations go to volunteers who respond, clean the area, and submit photo proof. Others can add donations to draw attention; paid requests are shown distinctly. There is also an option that only trash haul-away is needed.

title: Speed Cleanup: before/after photos, coins, volunteer hours letter
text: Speed Cleanup: you mark the place on the map, take a before photo, do the cleanup, then an after photo. Others see the result on the map and in good-news style feeds and can donate to you directly. You earn JoyCoins even without donations; coins can be redeemed with partners (list grows). Cleanup time is tracked; you can print an official-style letter about volunteer hours.

title: Event: schedule, chat, donations to participants, share link
text: Event is for planned cleanups, tree planting, and similar activities. You set place, time, and description; people can join. Like other requests, there is a participant chat and donations that go to cleanup participants. You can share the event link to social networks and messengers to attract volunteers.

title: Stripe in profile, routes to requests, notifications within ~10 miles
text: During registration you can connect Stripe to receive donations; the setup link appears in your profile. You can build a route to points that have requests. Users within about a 10-mile radius can receive notifications about relevant requests (wording may vary by build/region).

title: Physical presence, geolocation, in-app photos to finish work
text: Work for verification and completion is tied to being physically present and using geolocation. You cannot complete the work without live photos taken through the app as required by the flow. This supports fair verification of cleanups.

title: Share requests, search, social links on profile
text: Event and other requests can be shared to messengers and social networks via a built-in share action. You can search requests by address and by user—useful when influencers or communities organize cleanups. In profile you can add social links; user activity can be visible to others depending on settings.

title: Profile: requests, donations total, hours, print letter, QR for coins
text: Profile shows your requests and completed work, total donations received, volunteer hours, a button to print a volunteer-hours letter, and a QR flow for spending JoyCoins. JoyCoins can be exchanged for discounts at partner businesses.

title: Why people return: motivation layers in JoyPick
text: JoyPick combines several motivation layers: community (people see others, chat, join group cleanups), social recognition (sharing achievements), JoyCoins and donations (including donations attached to polluted spots on the map so the problem and reward stay visible), reporting polluted areas, volunteer hours tracking for school/work, and positive news for inspiration. The goal is to turn one-off goodwill into a lasting habit.

title: How cleanup verification works: distance check, photos, moderator
text: Volunteer arrives at the marked location and starts through the app. Geolocation is checked—if they are too far from the designated point (on the order of tens of meters, e.g. about 50 meters), the app warns and blocks starting the task. After cleanup, required photos are taken in the app and the user completes the task; finishing without being there and without those photos is not possible. A moderator then reviews the submission; after approval, held donations are distributed to recipients via Stripe (Joy Pick does not accumulate that float on its own balance—hold then direct distribution).

title: Moderation: manual first, dataset for models, possible community helpers
text: Moderation is manual for now, done by trusted people and the team when needed. Verified cleanups help build a quality dataset for future automated checks. Longer term, community-based moderation may be considered: active volunteers could get moderation roles; admin tooling may already support assigning such roles for selected users.

title: Reporting a polluted spot without being a volunteer first
text: You do not need to be a verified volunteer to report a polluted area. After installing the app you can immediately mark a dirty spot, attach a photo, and describe the issue—this is part of the core experience and helps populate the map even in quiet regions.

title: How volunteers can receive money: donations and payouts
text: Volunteers can receive money from donations attached to cleanup requests. Other users donate to fund a cleanup; after you complete the work, pass verification (location and in-app photos where required), and a moderator approves it, held donation funds can be credited to your balance. Set up Stripe from your profile to withdraw (instant payout or scheduled options, as shown in the app). These are voluntary peer-to-peer transfers for real cleanups—not a salary or wage paid by Joy Pick as an employer. You can also earn JoyCoins and accumulate volunteer hours shown in your profile.

title: What you can get for cleanups
text: For verified cleanups you can receive: donation money from other users (after moderation approval, funds go to your balance; withdraw via Stripe once connected), JoyCoins for verified work, and volunteer hours with an option to print an official-style hours letter from your profile. For Event-type requests, participants may receive donations according to that request’s rules.

title: Volunteer hours tracking and official letter
text: The app tracks time spent on verified cleanups as volunteer hours. In your profile you can print a letter documenting your hours on an official-style form. This supports school, work, or other programs that require documented volunteer time.

title: Donation holds: if the request is not completed, donor funds
text: Donation payments are placed on hold when paid. If the request with those donations is not completed under the app rules, the hold is released: funds return to the payer (the donor). Do not claim money «stays on the Joy Pick platform» or «is not returned automatically» instead of this flow, and do not hand-wave with «platform policy» for this case. Joy Pick does not accumulate users’ money as a platform cash pile: funds sit in hold within the payment stack (Stripe), and after the approved flow donors’ held amounts are distributed straight to recipients via Stripe—not parked on a Joy Pick balance in between.

title: Donation (= paid) request: map icon and list total
text: In the app, a request with money attached is called a donation request; in plain language it matches what people call a «paid» request. That applies if a donation was set when creating the request, or as soon as the first donation arrives later. On the map such a request shows a dollar icon. In the list view the app shows the total of all donations for that request. See the in-app Help section for more detail.

title: Share a request: deeplink, app installed or stores
text: To tell others about a request by sharing a link, use Share from request details. The link is a deeplink: if Joy Pick is installed, that request opens; if not, the user is prompted to download the app and is sent to the app stores. This is different from «create a new request».

title: Connect Stripe — in-app flow only
text: «How do I connect Stripe in my profile» refers to the profile/payouts area where Stripe Connect onboarding runs inside the app (per on-screen UI). Do not refuse with «I cannot help create a Stripe account»—the user is asking for the in-app payout setup, not bypassing the app to sign up on stripe.com alone.

title: Balance and «which bank»
text: Payout balance in the app is tied to connected Stripe Connect: withdrawals go to the card/account the user sets during Stripe onboarding—not a separate «Joy Pick bank account» in the everyday sense. Exact payout details appear in Stripe / profile after you connect.

title: Several Event participants—how donations are split
text: For Events, donation totals are split evenly across participants who have Stripe Connect connected: take the full donated amount and divide by the count of participants with Stripe. Participants without Stripe connected are not included in that divisor. If the user asks about an unfulfilled request, do not substitute this split answer—use the donor hold-release chunk instead. Do not invent other percentages: for Event participants it is equal shares among Stripe-connected participants.

title: Help: map card border colors and gray circle
text: The in-app Help (UI Guide) explains map markers. Border color on the request card: green—requests you created; orange—requests you joined/participate in; yellow—requests you donated to; purple—approved Event or Speed Cleanup within 7 days of creation where donations are still accepted; black—other requests. A gray circle around the map icon means the request is overdue, approved, or completed. A green dollar sign under the icon marks a donation-backed request.

title: Help: orange vs yellow donation amount chips
text: Per Help copy: the orange donation chip shows the total raised on your own request; after you finish the work and a moderator approves, funds move to your connected Stripe account (minus fees). The yellow chip shows totals donated by the community plus the creator; after approval, funds go to the performer (minus fees). Point users to Help for the visual reference.

title: Help: home top bar and profile block icons
text: Per Help: Chat opens chats with request creators and participants; red badge is unread count. Refresh reloads requests on the map and in the list. News is the Joy Pick feed; orange icon and pulsing dot mean new items. Wallet shows withdrawable balance and opens payouts. In the profile block: List icon opens completed requests (Coins) or payout history (Payouts); Exchange opens a partner QR to spend JoyCoins (Coins block); Pay Out opens payouts to withdraw balance (Payouts block).

title: Help: incomplete-request banner on home
text: When Home shows a banner about an incomplete cleanup (waste, speed cleanup, or event), the user can complete it or dismiss the reminder. If they cancel, the incomplete item is removed from the device but can still be finished later from request details—as stated in the banner copy inside the app.

title: Help: tree and truck icons on a card
text: Per the in-app Help (UI Guide): the Plant Tree indicator appears when an Event includes tree planting—shows a tree icon inside a white circle on the card. Trash Pickup Only means only haul-away is needed, no cleanup work—shows a truck icon in a white circle. These are extra markers on a request; users can see the visuals in Help inside the app.

title: What Joy Pick is for and what you can do in the app
text: Joy Pick is an app for environmental cleanups and volunteer actions. You see requests and events on a map. You can create a Waste Location (report pollution), Speed Cleanup (quick cleanup with before/after photos), or Event (scheduled cleanup or gathering). The app supports donations, JoyCoins, volunteer hours, chats on requests, and profile payouts via Stripe. The goal is to help clean polluted areas and motivate volunteers.
